correctness.rationale: For odd prime p, H_p=F_p³ with (a,b,c)(u,v,w)=(a+u,b+v,c+w+av), Fourier coset averaging is p times projector P_{ρ,L} on each irrep fixed vector. Injectivity iff selected fixed spaces span in every irrep. The p² one-dimensional characters force covering all p+1 projective quotient lines for a center-free design; central subgroup has zero fixed space in each p-dimensional Schrödinger irrep and at least p noncentral directions are then needed, so p+1 is globally minimal. In each Schrödinger rep, fixed vector of finite slope and lift c is v_{s,c}(t)=ζ^(−k(ct+s t(t−1)/2)), and vertical direction gives coordinate δ_{−c}. Pick S of (p+1)/2 slopes at c=0, complement at c=1, any vertical lift. The involution t↦1−t partitions coordinates into even dimension (p+1)/2 and odd (p−1)/2; q(t)=t(t−1)/2 has distinct orbit values. Two square matrices reduce to Chebotarev prime Fourier minors, nonzero for all k, proving complete span and at least p*binom(p,(p+1)/2) labeled designs. All zero lifts fail for p>=5 because p finite vectors are even and one vertical vector cannot span full p. Independent GF2 coset-incidence row rank checked all 3 splits at p=3 and all 10 splits at p=5, each rank p³. GF2 full rank implies complex full rank in these finite cases only; general proof is analytic.
